rubrics.justification: Description is consistent with a good-quality expanded blastocyst and matches the provided 3AA grade, with appropriate comments on ICM, TE, and thinning zona. However, some image-specific details such as exact ICM position and 'no obvious vacuolization/lysis' are somewhat overconfident from a single static image.

Integrates age, BMI, uterine factor, endometrial thickness, smoking, ovarian response, prior cycle history, and sperm parameters well with embryo quality. Minor limitation is that AMH is unavailable and the uterine factor is discussed somewhat generically.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong embryo and favorable age/endometrium balanced against smoking and uterine factor. Slight overstatement occurs in calling 3AA the 'highest' grade and in the confidence of the implantation baseline.

Recommendations are broadly aligned with IVF practice: SET in a young patient with a good-quality day-5 blastocyst, attention to uterine cavity assessment, luteal support, and lifestyle counseling. PGT-A suggestion is somewhat more debatable in a 31-year-old first cycle and not universally guideline-driven.

Provides practical next steps including SET, smoking cessation, review of uterine evaluation, luteal support, and cryopreservation planning. Useful and case-relevant, though some recommendations could be more specific to the exact uterine diagnosis and transfer protocol.
